papers.title: Unsupervised functional stage detection from EEG using topological data analysis.
papers.summary: Introduces a topological data analysis (TDA) feature engineering approach for unsupervised EEG functional stage detection, including a quick state-detecting algorithm (QSDA). Applied to meditation and sleep EEG, TDA-derived features produced well-separated stage boundaries and appeared to complement or outperform spectral features in some settings.

papers.title: A Proof-of-Concept Study of Weakly Supervised Labeling of Fine-Grained EEG Components for Artifact Attenuation
papers.summary: Introduces a weakly supervised framework combining a frequency-aware high-dimensional representation with Multi-Instance Learning to detect fine-grained EMG artifact components in EEG scalp recordings, enabling score-guided attenuation without component-level ground truth. Held-out-subject experiments show informative intra-component scores and the strongest reduction of artifact-related spectral deviations for jaw tension, with moderate effects for eyebrow raising and limited effects for frowning.

papers.title: The NeuroHab: A Low-Cost, Integrated System for Investigation of Neural Correlates of Behaviors.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Presents NeuroHab, an integrated low-cost (~$1,400) open-source operant conditioning system with solenoid-actuated capacitive lickports, FED3 food reward, conditioned-stimulus modules, and a central controller logging event timestamps at sub-millisecond latency (typically 56-728 μs). The system was deployed in over 50 behavior trials and more than 20 sessions with a Mini two-photon microscope, enabling millisecond-scale alignment of behavior with two-photon imaging and electrophysiology.

papers.title: High-frequency oscillations arise through distinct mechanisms in models of α- synucleinopathy and channelopathy-induced epilepsy.
papers.summary: Compares cortical high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 250-500 Hz) and interictal spikes in surface EEG from a transgenic α-synucleinopathy model (A53T mice, features of dementia with Lewy bodies) and a channelopathy-induced epilepsy model (Kcna1-/- mice). Both models showed elevated HFOs versus controls, with A53T mice exhibiting more HFOs and spikes, higher HFO frequency, longer duration, and non-REM-sleep predominance, suggesting distinct generation mechanisms and supporting HFOs as a potential biomarker for neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: The effects of temporal smoothing and interpolation on EEG microstate parameters, syntax, and our view of resting-state brain dynamics
papers.summary: Systematically examines how parametric temporal smoothing and GFP peak interpolation affect EEG microstate sequence parameters in eyes-closed resting-state recordings from 201 healthy subjects. Widening smoothing windows increased microstate duration and decreased occurrence rate, suppressed asymmetry and non-equilibrium dynamics, and strongly altered entropy rate and excess entropy; windows above 30 ms produced a memoryless, aperiodic, time-reversible first-order Markov picture, leading the authors to recommend avoiding intense smoothing.

papers.title: Applying pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic concepts from human clinical anesthesia to laboratory animal anesthesia.
papers.summary: Reviews how pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) concepts from human clinical anesthesia, using propofol as an example, can inform anesthetic depth assessment and drug administration in laboratory animal anesthesia. Argues that PK/PD simulation should support rather than replace physiological monitoring and separate assessment of hypnosis and nociception, accounting for species differences and helping standardize experiments and support animal welfare.

papers.title: Feature-Engineering Strategies for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children: A Controlled Benchmark of Expert, LLM-Guided and Full-Space Comparators
papers.summary: Benchmarks expert, LLM-guided, and full-space EEG feature strategies for pediatric ADHD classification under leakage-controlled subject-level validation. Expert-reconstructed features achieved the highest accuracy and balanced accuracy for every classifier, while LLM-guided selection showed no consistent advantage; a 200 V artifact gate reduced accuracy below the no-information rate.

papers.title: Exploring the Reconfiguration Effects of Physical Fatigue on the Gradient Space of Brain Function Based on EEG.
papers.summary: Using three embedding methods (PCA, Laplacian eigenmaps, diffusion maps) on resting-state EEG from 30 men before and after exhaustive treadmill exercise, physical fatigue reorganised low-dimensional functional-connectivity gradients in frequency-, region-, component-, and method-specific ways. PCA beta-band central G1 increase correlated with exercise duration (r=0.50, p=0.004), while alpha-band occipital displacement and theta-band eigenvalue changes differed between methods.

papers.title: Multimodal LLMs Can Learn to Read Brain Signals: A Vision--Language Model for Unified Multi-Task EEG Decoding
papers.summary: Introduces BraVista, a visual-language framework that encodes multichannel EEG as structured images and fine-tunes a general-domain vision-language model for unified multi-task EEG decoding without large-scale EEG pretraining. It achieves strong performance on sleep staging, emotion recognition, cognitive workload classification, and abnormal EEG detection across four datasets, and shows performance degrades under increasing noise, indicating reliance on EEG-relevant information.

papers.title: Distilling Trial-Level EEG Variability into Participant Representations: Neurophysiologically Constrained Graph Learning in ADHD
papers.summary: Develops a spatiotemporal graph attention network with ERP-informed temporal windows, phase-synchrony graph priors, and trial-to-participant transfer learning to analyze Go/NoGo EEG in children and adolescents with and without ADHD. It finds no reliable spatial attention differences between groups but extracts compact participant-level embeddings that retain diagnostic information beyond convolutional representations and exceed CNN performance.

papers.title: Neural signatures of auditory distraction and cognitive demand during working memory performance.
papers.summary: Investigates combined effects of auditory distraction and time pressure on working memory using multidimensional EEG in 30 healthy participants, finding distinct oscillatory signatures: distraction linked to widespread alpha suppression and frontal/parietal delta increases, time pressure to frontal/parietal theta increases, and the combined condition showing a non-additive spatial pattern. Beta asymmetry emerges as the most consistent hemispheric marker across conditions, while functional connectivity shows no significant condition-dependent effects.

papers.title: CADENCE: Open-source software for signal conditioning, feature extraction, visualization and analysis of cardiac optical mapping data
papers.summary: Presents CADENCE, an open-source MATLAB-based application for end-to-end processing, analysis, and visualization of cardiac optical mapping data, including denoising, conduction velocity, alternans, and rotor features. Validated against three blinded experts across four species and three tissue preparations, it achieved agreement comparable to inter-observer variability and recovered dominant frequency with a median error of 0.03% across 84/88 paced recordings.

papers.title: Spectrally-resolved transfer entropy in resting-state SEEG reveals epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic communication in adults and children with refractory epilepsy.
papers.summary: Characterizes directed, spectrally-resolved communication between seizure onset zones (SOZ) and non-involved zones using resting-state SEEG transfer entropy in adults and children with refractory epilepsy. Finds multiplex cross-frequency interactions, with longer NIZ-to-SOZ delays in adults and distinct SOZ-to-SOZ spectral patterns between cohorts.

papers.title: From emotional inhibition to memory suppression: Acute exercise modulates electrophysiological dynamics associated with inhibitory control during suppression of negative memories.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: Acute moderate-intensity exercise selectively modulated late-stage (2400–3000 ms) neural activity during suppression of negative memories, with effects over central and left parietal sites and alpha/beta power changes at the left parieto-occipital junction, accompanied by reduced intrusion frequency.

papers.title: Developmental variation in resting-state EEG spectral correlates of response inhibition in children and adolescents.
papers.summary: In 1654 children and adolescents, resting-state EEG spectral power and band-ratio indices correlated with response inhibition: higher delta, theta, and theta/beta ratio predicted poorer inhibition, while higher alpha, beta, alpha/theta, and beta/theta predicted better inhibition; age moderated several of these associations.

papers.title: Scaling subjects in cross-modal alignment: video decoding with EEG foundation model
papers.summary: Training a cross-modal EEG–video contrastive encoder on a cohort an order of magnitude larger than prior work revealed that subject scaling yields log-linear gains above ~50 subjects, with an EEG foundation model initialisation scaling ~1.6× faster per cohort doubling than random initialisation.

papers.title: Altered Aperiodic EEG Activity in Adolescents with Neurofibromatosis Type 1
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state EEG aperiodic exponent (1/f) in 16 adolescents with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and 16 matched neurotypical controls, finding a higher aperiodic exponent in the NF1 group, consistent with increased inhibitory tone. The NF1 group also showed lower dominant oscillatory frequency, with no significant association between aperiodic exponent and cognitive performance.

papers.title: Neural latent representation of implicit perceptual decision confidence signatures from brain-wide intracranial EEG
papers.summary: Machine learning applied to brain-wide intracranial EEG without explicit confidence reports identified robust low-dimensional neural latent representations of implicit perceptual decision confidence, with frontal spatiotemporal components distinguishing correctness, difficulty, and speed, and trajectories in a shared subspace improving distinguishability.

papers.title: Kinestesia: the prefrontal EEG response to a cognitive-motor intervention is graded by baseline cognitive status.
papers.summary: This companion neurophysiological study of the Kinestesia cognitive-motor intervention analyzed resting-state EEG before and after 30 sessions in 19 older adults (10 healthy controls, 9 with mild cognitive impairment). Eight of eleven prespecified EEG indices showed a Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected association with baseline MoCA, with the strongest effects for the Engagement Index and Alpha/Beta Ratio at Fp2, indicating that the electrocortical response was graded by baseline cognitive status.

papers.title: Vibrotactile transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) during working memory: convergent electrophysiological evidence for cortical efficiency
papers.summary: Active vibrotactile taVNS reduced scalp visual ERPs and temporal high-gamma responses during working memory compared to sham, with smaller ERPs associated with successful encoding in the hardest condition, supporting a cortical-efficiency rather than sensory-amplification mechanism.

papers.title: Music-evoked EEG signals for mental health assessment using two- and three-class classification.
papers.summary: This preliminary study used EEG recordings during music and no-music sessions with 48 participants to classify mental fatigue, anxiety, depression, and stress using a deep residual MLP. Binary mental fatigue classification achieved 72.92% accuracy in the music condition vs. 58.33% without music, and multi-output stress classification reached 93.75% accuracy but low AUC due to class imbalance.

papers.title: Intracranial electrophysiology reveals distinct neural representations of nociception and salience in the human brain
papers.summary: Using high-resolution intracranial recordings from 13 neurosurgical patients (2,018 electrodes), this study found that neural representations of nociception and salience are anatomically and functionally distinct: 77% of nociception-encoding electrodes did not encode low-probability sounds. Nociceptive representations occurred in posterior insula, inferior parietal, and perirolandic cortex, preceded salience representations by 120 ms, and intracranial stimulation near them more often caused sensory experience.

papers.title: Integrating resting-state functional connectivity, mismatch negativity, and auditory steady-state responses reveals convergent neurophysiological biomarkers of schizophrenia.
papers.summary: This retrospective secondary analysis of the African Schizophrenia EEG Dataset (153 participants) integrated resting-state functional connectivity, mismatch negativity (MMN), and auditory steady-state responses (ASSR) in a graph attention network. The multimodal framework achieved 91.8% balanced accuracy and 0.96 AUC for classifying schizophrenia, outperforming individual EEG models, with global efficiency, MMN peak amplitude, and ASSR inter-trial phase coherence as top predictive features.

papers.title: Vitamin B6 augments antidepressant activity of venlafaxine by restoring cortical EEG oscillations, behavior and oxidative biomarkers in chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced model of depression-like behavior.
papers.summary: This study tested whether Vitamin B6 enhances venlafaxine's antidepressant effects in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model, using 72 mice treated for 28 days. Combined treatment restored behavior, reduced oxidative stress markers (decreased MDA, increased catalase), and restored cortical EEG oscillations by attenuating theta hyperactivity and increasing alpha and gamma power, suggesting a promising combination strategy for stress-related depression.

papers.title: Acceleration of vision changes object representations from infancy to adulthood
papers.summary: Using frequency-tagging EEG with rapid serial visual presentation, this study quantified that object categorization in 4- and 9-month-old infants is seven times and two to three times slower than in adults, respectively. Presenting accelerated visual streams to adults and using deep convolutional neural networks showed that acceleration compromises fine-grained object distinction while sparing broad object representations, suggesting slow vision is a design feature of early development.

papers.title: Age-related differences in neural activity and functional connectivity during self- and other-referential processing: An EEG study.
papers.summary: In younger and older adults, EEG revealed lower P1 amplitudes and reduced directed connectivity in older adults during self- and other-referential processing, while self-related traits elicited a larger late positive potential (LPP) in older compared to younger adults.

papers.title: Tri-Stream Disentangled Network with Adaptive Dual-Space Fusion for Electroencephalography-Based Image Reconstruction on THINGS-EEG2.
papers.summary: Presents a reproducible protocol for EEG-based image reconstruction using a Tri-stream Disentangled Network (TDE-Net) with adaptive dual-space fusion on THINGS-EEG2. Across 10 participants, TDE-Net achieved a mean CLIP pairwise identification accuracy of 0.8135, with ablation analyses characterizing the contributions of graph and semantic streams.

papers.title: Oscillatory dynamics within fronto-insular-parietal networks integrate thermosensory signals into body ownership.
papers.summary: Combined multisensory illusion, thermal imaging, and EEG to study oscillatory correlates of skin-temperature changes during altered body ownership. Decreased hand temperature during ownership modulation was tracked by theta/low-alpha activity in right premotor regions, and frontoparietal connectivity including insula was associated with temperature changes coupled with ownership modulation.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of uncertain decision-making in anxious adolescents: an EEG study based on the balloon analogue risk task.
papers.summary: Anxious adolescents (n=20) and matched controls (n=20) performed a gain/loss Balloon Analogue Risk Task during EEG. Anxious adolescents showed behavioral avoidance (fewer pumps, lower BART scores) and distinct neural dynamics: elevated beta-band power and occipito-temporal connectivity during gain decisions, and increased theta-band parieto-temporal connectivity in loss contexts.

papers.title: Determination of central pain modulation biomarkers to characterise patients with cancer and refractory pain: protocol for a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional case-control study protocol aims to identify central pain modulation biomarkers in cancer patients with and without refractory pain using quantitative sensory testing (QST) and EEG, with planned recruitment of at least 470 participants to characterize pain perception and modulation.

papers.title: EEG predictors of transition from clinical high risk to psychotic disorders: A systematic review with implications for data harmonisation.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found that duration mismatch negativity (MMN) and P3b event-related potential amplitudes were significantly reduced in clinical high-risk individuals who transitioned to psychosis compared to non-transitioners, though heterogeneity and methodological variability limit predictive utility.

papers.title: Phase-dependent oscillatory dynamics during needle retention and withdrawal: a comparison of penetrating and non-penetrating acupuncture.
papers.summary: In a 2x2 crossover EEG study with 20 acupuncture-naive participants, verum and sham acupuncture both increased central theta and beta power during needle retention and reduced alpha power post-withdrawal, with the most consistent difference being a weaker alpha reduction for sham compared to verum acupuncture.

papers.title: GIRK Channel Loss of Function Increases Dendritic Excitability in a Mouse Model of GNB1 Encephalopathy.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In a mouse model of GNB1 encephalopathy (Gnb1 p.I80T mutation), hippocampal neurons exhibited simplified dendritic morphology, reduced GABA_B receptor-mediated synaptic inhibition, and increased dendritic excitability with longer calcium spikes, which were reversed by the GIRK channel activator ML297.

papers.title: Neurophysiological signatures of latent brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: integrating EEG, cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG.
papers.summary: Narrative review examining EEG, NIRS/cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG/BIS as objective perioperative neuromonitoring markers for brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND). Suggests that reduced/slowed alpha activity, lower spectral edge frequency, altered theta activity, burst suppression, cerebral oxygen desaturation burden, rSO2 variability, and prolonged deep anesthesia may reflect different dimensions of vulnerability, but current evidence is limited and these are candidate markers rather than validated early-warning tools.

papers.title: Indoor environmental conditions and interictal epileptiform discharge frequency during pediatric video-EEG monitoring.
papers.summary: Continuous minute-level indoor temperature and humidity were correlated with interictal epileptiform discharge frequency in 50 pediatric epilepsy patients during video-EEG monitoring. Significant individual-level correlations with temperature and humidity were found in 37/50 patients each, with highly heterogeneous bidirectional effects, while group-level GLMM showed only a significant circadian effect on discharge rates and no significant environmental or clinical moderation.

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles
papers.summary: The authors designed and tested 3D-printed hair-anchored EEG electrode attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured hairstyles in 17 healthy adults, comparing them with conventional cap electrodes. Novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance, decreased disconnection rates from 20% to 0.1%, and improved signal quality without reducing comfort.

papers.title: Multimodal neuromonitoring-guided cerebral protection and early neurocognitive outcomes after aortic arch surgery.
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort study (n=186) evaluated whether a multimodal neuromonitoring-guided cerebral-protection protocol was associated with lower cerebral physiological burden and improved early neurocognitive outcomes after open aortic arch surgery. The guided cohort had lower rSO2 burden, shorter EEG suppression, and shorter impaired autoregulation duration, with lower odds of postoperative delirium (OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.17-0.77) and 30-day cognitive decline (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.13-0.75).

papers.title: Noninvasive Intelligent Brain-Metasurface System for Real-Time Electromagnetic Wave Manipulation.
papers.summary: A noninvasive intelligent brain-computer interface was integrated with a reconfigurable metasurface to enable real-time electromagnetic wave manipulation from decoded motor-imagery EEG and EOG commands. The system achieved beam steering, polarization conversion, and radar cross-section reduction, with a peak gain of 18.54-19.29 dBi, 3 dB beamwidth of 12°-15° at +20° steering, and >10 dB RCS reduction across 3.7-3.85 GHz.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Diagnosis: Protocol for a Scoping Review.
papers.summary: Describes a scoping review protocol to map AI, machine learning, and deep learning approaches for ADHD diagnosis, covering data modalities, validation practices, and interpretability. The review will follow PRISMA-ScR and JBI guidelines, searching five databases for studies from January 2019 to April 2026.

papers.title: Neurosyphilis presenting as status epilepticus and hemiplegia diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing: A case report.
papers.summary: A case of neurosyphilis initially misdiagnosed as acute cerebral infarction presented with status epilepticus and hemiplegia. Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing identified Treponema pallidum, and EEG showed persistent periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges despite anti-syphilitic and antiepileptic therapy.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
